money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of Hungary is the Forint (HUF). Euros (EUR) may be accepted at certain places in major cities. Credit and debit cards are widely accepted, but some businesses may only accept cash. Only change money at banks or other authorised dealers or withdraw cash from ATMs. Most banks have ATMs that accept major international cards. Check all banknotes received are valid. Some outdated notes are still in circulation. Declare funds of more than EUR 10,000 or equivalent if you're travelling between Hungary and a non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not just cash. Failure to do so

laws.rule: Don't use or carry illegal drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe. Possessing even small amounts of illegal drugs, including marijuana, can lead to prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Local authorities can ask to see your identification at any time. Carry your passport at all times. A photocopy won't be accepted. Smoking is banned: on all public transport and at transport stops in Budapest within 5 metres of entrances to education buildings in restaurants, bars and cafes Large fines apply. Heavy fines exist for minor driving infringements. Penalties for serious driving offences include prison.

laws.rule: For specific information on bringing medication into Hungary, read more National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition website.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: You can drive on your Australian driver's licence for 1 year if you also have either: a Hungarian translation of your licence, or an International Driving Permit (IDP) Get your IDP before your travel.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Same-sex relationships are legal and laws prohibit sexual discrimination. However, homosexuality isn't widely accepted. Public displays of affection may draw unwanted attention. Hungary passed legislation that could provide a legal basis to ban LGBTQIA+ pride events. Authorities can use facial recognition technology to identify and fine anyone who takes part in illegal or banned demonstrations. Harassment and violence against LGBTQIA+ people have occurred. Monitor media reporting and follow the advice of local authorities. Visit Hungary: be polite and punctual, use a handshake in formal settings, and validate public transport tickets before travelling. Tipping is customary at about 10% unless a service charge is included.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Hungary is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register and footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
